title: Probabilistic semantics of a copy operation
statement: Let $N$ be a finite nondeterministic Turing machine, let $os$ be a Boolean, let $x$ be a Boolean word, and let $B$ be a natural number. For a copy type $k$, let $r_{\mathrm{src}}(k)$ and $r_{\mathrm{dst}}(k)$ denote its source and destination register indices, and let $q_k$ be its exit label. Suppose a register state $\sigma$ has every register at most $B$, its scratch value $z$ is zero, and the sum of its source and destination register values is at most $B$. Suppose also that $\sigma'$ has register vector obtained from that of $\sigma$ by replacing the destination value with the sum of the source and destination values. If the configuration at label $q_k$ with register state $\sigma'$ has probabilistic semantics with probability $p$, then the configuration at the initial copy label for $k$ with register state $\sigma$ has probabilistic semantics with probability $p$.

Let $N$ be a finite-state nondeterministic Turing machine, let $x$ be a Boolean word,
and let $B$ be a natural number. For a copy type $k$, write $r_{\mathrm{src}}(k)$ and
$r_{\mathrm{dst}}(k)$ for its designated source and destination registers, and $q_k$ for
its exit label. Suppose the register tuple $\sigma$ has every register at most $B$ and
its scratch register $z$ is zero. If the sum of the values in $r_{\mathrm{src}}(k)$ and
$r_{\mathrm{dst}}(k)$ is at most $B$, and the register vector of $\sigma'$ is obtained
from that of $\sigma$ by replacing the destination value with this sum, then for any
rational $p$, probabilistic semantics with probability $p$ at label $q_k$ and tuple
$\sigma'$ implies probabilistic semantics with probability $p$ at the initial copy label
for $k$ and tuple $\sigma$.
